title: Remote monitoring after cardiac surgery across four centres: effect and cost-effectiveness
subtitle: Ministry funding decision for 2028
statement: Two of four cardiac surgery centres adopted 30-day remote monitoring after discharge in March 2025, at about 1,400 per patient; the other two use usual follow-up. About 14 percent of patients are readmitted within 30 days. The ministry must decide whether to fund monitoring at all centres from 2028 and needs its effect on readmissions, emergency visits and costs, estimated fairly when centres chose whether to adopt it and differ in case mix and volume.
whoAffected: Adults discharged after cardiac surgery in four centres, their carers, monitoring nurses, and the ministry as payer.
whatHurts: Readmissions and emergency visits in the first weeks after surgery are common and costly; funding an ineffective programme would divert money, while not funding an effective one would leave preventable readmissions.
currentPractice: Remote monitoring at A and B since March 2025; telephone call at one week and clinic at six weeks at C and D.
whyNow: The ministry's 2028 funding decision needs an answer by June 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients recover at home safely after cardiac surgery, with problems caught early and fewer returns to hospital.
summary: Problem framed as an effect and cost question for a funding decision; constraints omitted by the model.
